posts.t:
I will be posting less trades going forward, as I will be moving towards more quality swing type trades, rather that the SAS I have been practicising of late. There should be a large enough sample of trades here now in my journal to learn from anyway. I would encourage all to start and maintain a journal if you are not doing so already. It will help your learning and also leave nuggets behind for others to draw from. You never know which of your posts will set some trader on that AHA! trail. Many times it is just how YOU express or draw something in a post or on a chart, that makes the difference from the same thing that has been said a hundred times before!

I wrote this in my very first post: " As the great Zig Zigler wrote " You'll get what you want when you've helped enough people get what they want"."

This one below was easy to see and take!

از این به بعد کمتر معامله پست می‌کنم، چون به سمت معامله‌های سوینگ باکیفیت‌تر می‌روم، نه SAS‌هایی که اخیراً تمرین می‌کردم. به‌هرحال الآن نمونهٔ به‌اندازهٔ کافی بزرگی از معامله‌ها در ژورنالم برای یادگیری هست. همه را تشویق می‌کنم اگر ژورنال ندارید شروع کنید و نگهش دارید. به یادگیری‌تان کمک می‌کند و تکه‌های طلایی هم برای دیگران باقی می‌گذارد. هرگز نمی‌دانی کدام پستت معامله‌گری را روی مسیر آهای! می‌اندازد. خیلی وقت‌ها فقط این که تو چیزی را چطور بیان می‌کنی یا در پست یا روی چارت می‌کشی، تفاوت را می‌سازد با همان چیزی که صد بار قبل گفته شده!

این یکی پایین دیدن و گرفتنش آسان بود!

Thanks for the comments and markup, DrS! I've seen FO's mentioned here and there on RTM but I've only found 1 thread about them and the content was removed. Do you know where I can read more about them?

I think I get what a FO is, but knowing when to expect one is a bit unclear. From your chart it looks like you're saying that there were a bunch of sell orders at the area marked FTB, but highs you pointed at for 1 and 2 failed to trigger those sells. So at 2nd time back you entered because of the FO when looking left at 1 and 2 but it's really just triggering the sells that 1 and 2 failed to trigger from FTB. Kinda wordy but hopefully that made sense. If all that's true and made sense, is the trick to FO's to just look further left that the last high(es)? Anyway, any resources or input you can offer is much appreciated!

DrSwing wrote: Right third time lucky:)

Ok, this post is an insight into one method of how I try to find my trade opps.

I read the charts to find zone engulfs rather than just DBR/RBD engulfs as this gives the desired R:R.

I see the charts in terms of Poles and Flags and I'm looking to the SR transition level between the PAZs. This trade level has to be an M1 SD zone 3-4 pips wide and providing an FO to the above/below FTR/FL. I then trade the return to this level, giving me a potentially massive R:R. Some pics below to paint this picture.

This would be my main view

Dr swing, this post helped me greatly! as well as all your SAS. as others have said all this info is here but for some reason viewing your charts with the same info has sparked an awesome aha moment for me. I have so much more to learn but finally feel like my blinders have been removed. haha THANK YOU!!!

Are the gray boxes labeled 1,2,3, and 4 your targets, DrS? Or are you just planning to ride it down and let PA take you out?

The lighter color boxes are decisions I'm always a bit confused by, either with entry, exit, or just what to expect in general. At each one, price comes back and deeply retraces the base - does that weaken it or is it still a strong point given how price left? Since orders generated the move up, there must have still been a lot of buys to move price that far that quickly, but some of them had to be absorbed by the amount of time price spent there too.

Your ideas are appreciated but I think this is something I need to spend some time on too.

EDIT: I just realized that 2 is different than 3 or 4. At 2, price hadn't closed outside of the base whereas at 3 and 4 it left and came back. So at current I think 1 is stronger than 2 based on the time spent there, and 2 is stronger than 3 or 4 due to FTB having already occurred. Thoughts?

جعبه‌های رنگ روشن‌تر تصمیم‌هایی هستند که همیشه کمی گیجم می‌کنند، چه در ورود، چه خروج، چه انتظار کلی. در هر کدام، قیمت برمی‌گردد و عمیقاً بیس را مجدداً می‌پیماید — آیا این ضعیفش می‌کند یا با توجه به نحوهٔ ترک قیمت، هنوز نقطهٔ قوی است؟ چون سفارش‌ها حرکت بالا را ساختند، باید خرید زیادی بوده که قیمت را این‌قدر سریع آن‌قدر دور ببرد، اما بخشی از آن‌ها هم باید با مدت زمانی که قیمت آنجا مانده جذب شده باشد.
